lesson.title: Fair by design
lesson.subtitle: The total, the worst-off, and the price of fairness

video.title: Fair by design
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — education lecturer (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: Three ways to score a group

scenes.visual: Dr Farah beside the staff-room noticeboard: a rota with a big total at the bottom and one sad face.
scenes.animation: The total glows; then one name is circled.
scenes.narration: Last term our duty rota had the highest total happiness in the staff room. And Salma got the duty she hates most, every single week. Was that really the best rota?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: fairness by design, built into the model, not added at the end.

scenes.visual: Three cards: a calculator, a single person, a ruler between two people.
scenes.animation: Cards drop in as each measure is named.
scenes.on_screen_text: Three ways to score a group
scenes.narration: There’s more than one way to score a plan for a group. The total adds up everyone’s score. The worst-off looks only at the person doing worst. And the gap is the distance between the best-off and the worst-off.

scenes.visual: A bar chart of each teacher’s score under the best-total plan: 9, 8 and 2.
scenes.animation: Bars grow; Salma’s short bar turns red.
scenes.narration: Three teachers rate three duties from one to nine: the morning gate, the lunch hall and the library. The plan with the best total gives Amina the gate, Joseph the lunch hall and Salma the library: nineteen points. But Salma rates the library a two.

scenes.visual: The same chart redrawn: 6, 7 and 5, with a floor line at 5.
scenes.animation: Bars re-grow; a dashed floor line slides in at 5.
scenes.narration: Now change the goal: make the worst-off as well off as possible. Amina takes the library, Joseph the gate and Salma the lunch hall. The total drops to eighteen, but nobody scores below five.

scenes.visual: A big ‘19 → 18’ with a label underneath.
scenes.animation: The numbers flip; the label rises.
scenes.narration: The difference, one point here, is the price of fairness: what the total gives up so the worst-off does better. Often it’s small. Sometimes it’s large, and then people must decide together whether to pay it.

scenes.animation: Lines type themselves; the maximise line highlights.
scenes.narration: In a model, fairness is just a few more lines. Add a variable for the worst score. Say every teacher’s score is at least that, and maximise it.

scenes.visual: Mr Joseph holds up two rota cards, both stamped ‘floor 5’. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Two rotas both give the worst-off teacher five, the best floor there is. How should the solver choose between them?

scenes.visual: Three numbered steps appear one by one.
scenes.animation: Each step slides in as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: First the floor, then the total
scenes.narration: Keep the floor of five, then make the total as big as possible. Solvers do it in two steps. Solve for the best floor, fix it as a limit, and solve again for the total.

scenes.visual: A staff meeting: a rule written on a chart, scores pinned up beside it.
scenes.animation: The rule is written; scores pin up one by one.
scenes.narration: Which rule is fair isn’t for the modeller alone to decide. Ask the people affected which measure they want, before anyone sees the result. Write the rule down, publish the scores, and let people check them.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: a five-by-five table of scores, two totals side by side.
scenes.animation: A finger taps ‘Let them choose in turn’; the totals appear.
scenes.narration: In the app, give each class one teacher. Compare first come, first served with the best total. Then change Karim’s scores, and see who loses out.

scenes.visual: Dr Farah points at the rota on the noticeboard. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A rota has the best total, but one teacher gets the worst duty every week. What do you change in the model?

scenes.visual: Four summary lines and a takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Add a floor for everyone, then make the total as big as possible. Remember: the total, the worst-off and the gap measure different things. Fairness goes into the model as limits or goals. And agree the rule with the people affected, then publish it.

scenes.visual: Pupils in two groups with job cards; the board shows two totals and two lowest scores.
scenes.animation: Cards move; totals are written up.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: give groups a small table of how much three pupils like three class jobs. One group finds the best total; another makes the least happy pupil as happy as possible. Compare: what did fairness cost, and which plan would the class choose?

checkpoints.prompt: Two rotas give the worst-off teacher 5, the best floor there is. How should the solver choose?

options.text: Keep the floor of 5, then make the total as big as possible
Go back to the best total

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — fix the floor as a limit, then solve again for the total: fair first, then as good as possible for everyone.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — both plans are equally fair, but one may be better for everyone else. Keep the floor and then maximise the total.

checkpoints.prompt: A rota has the best total, but one teacher gets the worst duty every week. What do you change?

options.text: Nothing: the total is the best possible
Add a floor: every score at least a value, then the best total
Take that teacher off the rota

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a floor for everyone, then the best total, keeps the rota good and stops one person carrying the cost.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the best total hides who pays. Add a floor for every teacher, then make the total as big as possible.
